Batch: MiTeC Mail Checker bundled OpenSSL static follow-up

RetainedPayload.Interpretation: This static inspection does not prove whether the application dynamically loads the included OpenSSL DLLs or uses another network path.

Observations: OpenSSL's release timeline identifies 1.0.1e as released on 2013-02-11.
The 1.0.1 branch is out of support since 2017-01-01 and no longer receives updates.
OpenSSL 1.0.1e predates 1.0.1g; the official 1.0.1 vulnerability page says CVE-2014-0160 affected versions before 1.0.1g.
OpenSSL says all pre-3.0 releases use the dual OpenSSL and SSLeay license, including unsupported historical releases.
OpenSslPublisherEvidence.Limits: Version/company/banner resources identify an OpenSSL 1.0.1e build but do not prove the DLLs are byte-for-byte official release builds or identify their compiler/source modifications. A source-release listing is not a Windows DLL checksum or provenance record.

RemainingBlockers: The 1.0.1e branch is unsupported and predates fixes including CVE-2014-0160; actual Mail Checker exposure depends on runtime use and protocol behavior, which was not tested.
Exact binary provenance/build and any modifications are not established; the DLLs are unsigned and no separate upstream LICENSE file appears in the retained app file list.
The OpenSSL dual-license notice obligations and redistribution compliance for these binaries remain unresolved.
The application has no direct static import of the bundled OpenSSL DLL names; dynamic loading/use remains unknown.
Publisher terms, local entitlement, mail-account behavior, send/delete controls and isolated sink acceptance remain open.
Inspection: Recomputed installer and extracted member hashes; read PE imports, version resources, signatures and bounded ASCII strings only. No application or DLL ran, and no network/mail action occurred.
